description: Attack the big dense shapes 6/7/11 with a BLOCK one-sided Jacobi eigensolver expressed as batched tensor-core GEMM — distinct from the refuted two-sided cusolverDnSsyevjBatched (brief-58, 15ms/mat) and from the tridiag family. Partition columns into block-pairs; each sweep applies block Jacobi rotations that orthogonalize column-blocks via batched small dense eigendecompositions of the 2bx2b Gram sub-blocks + a batched GEMM column update A<-A@J (all tensor-core, no per-column tridiag sync). A few sweeps converge for the moderately-conditioned dense shapes; eigenvalues = converged column norms, eigenvectors = accumulated rotations. Per-matrix residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback. Measure sweeps-to-converge vs cuSOLVER 0.85ms/mat.

two-sided BLOCK JACOBI (batched tensor-core GEMM congruence A<-W^T A W) for n=512 dense-even shape 11, b=64 sweeps=8 3xTF32. Closest-to-identity 2bx2b eigenvector reordering FIXES convergence (torch.linalg.eigh's ascending-sort permutation cycles the sweep; minimal rotation converges quadratically 4-6 sweeps -> offF/AF 5e-6 on the INDEFINITE even spectrum). 39/39 validate, orth 1.9e-5 / eigr 1.4e-5 far under gates. Irreducible in pure torch: many small-contraction batched GEMMs + per-step gather/scatter + cuSOLVER sub-eigh don't amortize vs one fused syevd/matrix.

Built two-sided BLOCK JACOBI eigensolver as batched tensor-core GEMM (the correct formulation for the INDEFINITE dense-even spectrum -- one-sided/SVD-style only yields |lambda| and loses eigenvalue signs). Branch tip 691d25747 = parent geomean 28620 (route disabled; machinery retained). BEST reached: parent (block Jacobi regressed every config). 39/39 validate, stream absent (grep 0).

KEY WINS/FACTS measured: (1) CORRECTNESS SOLVED -- torch.linalg.eigh's ascending-sort permutes the 2bx2b eigenvector columns and CYCLES the sweep (offF/AF plateaus ~0.4, never converges); the fix is the CLOSEST-TO-IDENTITY minimal-rotation reorder (argsort of per-column dominant row + positive-diagonal sign), after which it converges quadratically. (2) SWEEPS-TO-CONVERGE (brief's key ask): n=512 even spectrum needs 6 sweeps (5 passes only ~half, eigr 2.3e-2>gate 9.2e-3); n=1024 needs 8. 3xTF32 sufficient (orth ~2e-5, eigr e-3..e-5 far under gates), TF32 also passes (Lerr ~3e-3).

WHY IT LOSES (profiled, GEMM/eigh-bound confirmed): NO config approaches cuSOLVER. shape11 n512b640 best 1080ms (b64 sw6) vs 99.8ms; shape7 n1024b60 915ms vs 112ms; 6-12x slower. Cost floor MAPPED per sweep (b640n512): sub-eigh cuSOLVER-syevd on 2bx2b dominates (2b=32 4.9ms/call, 2b=64 9.5, 2b=256 88), small-contraction congruence GEMM floor (b16 337/b32 153/b64 72/b128 33 ms/sweep), per-step gather/scatter 260ms/solve. b=64 best COMBINED ~180ms/sweep. The cuSOLVER 2bx2b eigh is itself the SIMT syevd we're escaping, and mega-med on tiny blocks measured SLOWER (15 vs 9.5ms). Root cause: block Jacobi's 40-250 separate batched ops/solve don't amortize vs cuSOLVER's ONE fused syevd/matrix.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not reached, could change the verdict): (a) FUSED CUSTOM MEGAKERNEL keeping a whole sweep resident (like _eigh_megakernel) to kill the per-step HBM round-trips + launch overhead + the cuSOLVER sub-eigh -- the only thing that could break the pure-torch floor, but a large nvcc effort the brief scoped out. (b) ONE-SIDED variant (~2/3 the GEMM: one col-update not row+col) -- but the 2bx2b Gram eigh still dominates so unlikely to break through; measure to confirm. (c) gather/scatter elimination by composing consecutive-step permutations (halves the 260ms) -- helps but eigh still dominates. (d) THRESHOLD/greedy pair selection to cut sweeps below 6. (e) a FUSED batched 2bx2b eigh primitive (Jacobi-in-registers) replacing cuSOLVER syevd -- the highest-leverage single change since sub-eigh is ~50-60% of cost. Recommend NOT spending more workers on pure-torch block Jacobi for these shapes unless (a)/(e) is pursued; the frontier for 6/7/11 is more likely the Chebyshev (brief-75) / resolvent (brief-78) lines or a fused kernel.

BUILT & MEASURED THE LEVER: fused resident-sweep block-Jacobi CUDA megakernel (bjac_fused_k): one CTA owns one matrix, A+V in global, the WHOLE sweep (p-1 steps x sweeps) runs in ONE launch, the 2bx2b sub-eigh is an in-SMEM PARALLEL cyclic Jacobi (chess-tournament, tb/2 disjoint pairs/round) -> NO cuSOLVER, NO per-op HBM materialization, NO gather/scatter, closest-to-identity reorder in-kernel. It is CORRECT: 39/39 validate, n=512 orth 1.9e-5 / eigr 5.7e-5 / Lerr 3e-6. But it hits the manager-anticipated ON-CHIP BARRIER/OCCUPANCY WALL. ncu (1 sweep, 1 subsweep, M=16): Duration 173.9ms, Compute SM throughput 1.25%, Memory throughput 6.2%, achieved occupancy 12.5% (theoretical 62.5%), 48 reg/thread, 33KB dyn smem. shape11 b640 = 26.3s (263x SLOWER than cuSOLVER 99.8ms), geomean 43822. Root cause: one-CTA-per-matrix caps parallelism at 16-640 CTAs on 148 SMs AND the sub-eigh's tb-1 sequential rounds each carry 3 __syncthreads -> a long dependency/barrier chain the SMs sit idle through. Sweeping b DOWN (16, 8) per the manager's suggestion did NOT help (~30s, and 6 sweeps stopped converging at more/smaller blocks: eigr 2.2e-2/4e-2 > gate).

CUDA GRAPHS RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT: on the torch path wall==gpu_event (1160.6 vs 1160.2ms, zero launch gap) -> the op-amortization wall is HBM-round-trip + kernel-compute, NOT launch overhead, so graph-capturing the fixed-topology sweep buys ~nothing. (The manager's cheaper-first-step hypothesis is disproved for this workload.)

THE FUNDAMENTAL TENSION (now fully mapped): the ~14ms HBM floor requires FULL fusion (eliminate the 692ms of torch gather/scatter+GEMM-materialization), but full fusion in one kernel caps at 1 CTA/matrix -> the 12.5%-occupancy barrier wall. Partial fusion (custom batched 2bx2b sub-eigh kernel + keep torch tensor-core GEMMs) is bounded BELOW by the measured torch GEMM+gather floor (b64: 72ms/sweep GEMM x6 + 260ms gather + finish ~= 692ms) -- above cuSOLVER even with a FREE sub-eigh. All three roads measured or tightly bounded to lose to cuSOLVER's single fused syevd/matrix.

ONE UNTRIED DIRECTION that could break the tension (needs manager decision -- large effort): a FUSED-PER-STEP batched kernel launched (p-1)xsweeps ~= 42 times, each launch a custom kernel that, batched across ALL M matrices with M*(p/2) CTAs (good occupancy), does BOTH the 2bx2b sub-eigh AND that step's congruence contribution for its block-pair -- no gather/scatter (index via the schedule inline), no GEMM materialization, sub-eigh in-register. This keeps occupancy high (thousands of CTAs) while cutting the gather/scatter+materialization that bounds the partial-fusion road; the residual cost is 42 launches (measured ~6ms total launch, negligible) + the per-step HBM congruence traffic (~HBM floor). It is the only design that simultaneously avoids BOTH the occupancy wall (many CTAs) and the materialization floor (fused). Whether the inter-step global barrier (= the 42 launches) plus the per-step block-row/col HBM traffic lands under 99.8ms is unmeasured -- worth one more brief if the manager wants to pursue block Jacobi further. Otherwise the frontier for shapes 6/7/11 is more likely the Chebyshev (brief-75) / resolvent (brief-78) lines. Recommend the manager weigh the fused-per-step kernel (uncertain, large) vs redirecting to those lines.

Bug fixed: row/col kernels needed cudaFuncSetAttribute for >48KB dynamic SMEM at b=64. 39/39 validate (n512 orth 1.9e-5, eigr 5e-5, Lerr 3e-6). RESULT: shape11 b640 = 6.44s (64x cuSOLVER 99.8ms), geomean 39372 -- better than fused-1CTA (26.3s) but still a big regression. ncu (b=32, one round) SUCCESSFULLY escaped the occupancy wall: achieved occupancy 72-92% (vs 12.5% for 1-CTA/matrix); congruence kernels near HBM-bound (row 2.89ms 88.7%mem 90.7%occ; col 11.52ms 71%mem 92%occ). THE NEW/FINAL WALL: bjac_subeigh_k = 116ms/round at 97.75% MEMORY throughput, 72.6% occ -- the in-SMEM parallel cyclic-Jacobi (tb-1=63 barrier-synced rounds x subsweeps) is SMEM-BANDWIDTH-bound and ~12x SLOWER than cuSOLVER's own batched syevd (which does the identical 5120x64x64 block eighs in 9.5ms). Congruence floor also ~14ms/round x ~120 rounds = ~1700ms (col kernel strided non-coalesced column gather at 71% mem). Per-solve pays congruence+subeigh traffic ~120x vs cuSOLVER's ONE fused syevd/matrix. subsweeps=1 (3077ms) does NOT converge (eigr 2.2e-2>gate); ss=2/sweeps=8 converges. THIRD CORNER MAPPED: good occupancy achieved, but (a) hand-rolled in-SMEM 2b sub-eigh loses 12x to cuSOLVER's syevd, (b) the per-step congruence re-reads block-rows/cols ~120x. ncu saved.

CORRECT: 39/39 validate, n512 orth 1.9e-5 / eigr 5e-5 / Lerr 3e-6.

THE OCCUPANCY WALL IS FIXED (the manager's premise held): ncu (b=32, one round) achieved occupancy 72-92% (vs 12.5% for the 1-CTA-per-matrix fused kernel). The congruence kernels are near-HBM-bound and cheap: bjac_row_k 2.89ms (88.7% mem, 90.7% occ), bjac_col_k 11.52ms (71% mem, 92% occ). So premises 1+2 (occupancy via many CTAs, ~free launches) both verified.

BUT TWO NEW WALLS surfaced (ncu-measured), so it is still 64x cuSOLVER (shape11 b640 = 6.44s, geomean 39372):
 (A) bjac_subeigh_k = 116ms/round at 97.75% MEMORY throughput -- the in-SMEM parallel cyclic-Jacobi (tb-1=63 barrier-synced rounds x subsweeps) is SMEM-BANDWIDTH-bound and ~12x SLOWER than cuSOLVER's OWN batched syevd (the identical 5120x64x64 block eighs run in 9.5ms). The manager's premise-3 hope that the in-register sub-eigh is ~free is disproved at 2b=64: hand-rolled Jacobi loses 12x to tuned syevd.
 (B) even swapping in cuSOLVER for the sub-eigh (hybrid, measured): lower bound 1346ms for JUST subeigh+gather across the 120 rounds (~11ms/round), + ~1700ms congruence = ~3000ms. The (p-1)*sweeps ~= 120 rounds is the fundamental multiplier: each round pays a per-block eigh + a full block-row/col HBM re-read/write, whereas cuSOLVER pays ONE fused syevd/matrix (156us/mat).

COMPLETE DESIGN-SPACE MAP (all corners, by measurement): torch multi-op (HBM/eigh-bound 1080ms) | fused 1-CTA/matrix (occupancy-bound 12.5%, 26.3s) | per-step B*(p/2)-CTA (occupancy-fixed 72-92% but sub-eigh SMEM-bound + 120x congruence, 6.44s) | hybrid (~3000ms floor). CUDA graphs ruled out (wall==gpu_event). The three corners trade the SAME conserved difficulty: full fusion hits the ~14ms HBM floor but 12.5% occupancy; per-step gets occupancy but pays 120 rounds of eigh+congruence; partial/hybrid is bounded by the 120-round multiplier. All realizable forms measured >13x cuSOLVER.

REMAINING OPEN KNOBS (manager's call): (a) a THRESHOLD/greedy Jacobi that skips already-small block-pairs to cut rounds below 120; (b) a custom FUSED-STEP kernel that processes ALL p/2 pairs of a step in one launch reading each element ONCE (removes the (p-1)x re-read within a sweep -> closer to the true per-sweep HBM floor) while keeping many CTAs -- the untried 4th point between full-fusion and per-pair; (c) FP16 storage of A to halve the congruence HBM. Whether any lands under 99.8ms is unmeasured. My measurements suggest the block-Jacobi line is heavily bounded on these shapes; I'd weight the manager toward the Chebyshev (brief-75)/resolvent (brief-78) lines for shapes 6/7/11, but the fused-per-STEP (not per-pair) kernel (b) is the one structural variant not yet built if the manager wants to keep pushing Jacobi.
